candidate_requirements.requirement: Identify the absence of a comparator/control group as the key missing information precluding comparative efficacy conclusions.
candidate_requirements.rationale: The task explicitly asks what can and cannot be concluded about comparative efficacy; without noting the missing comparator the appraisal is materially incomplete.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Framing as lack of randomisation or natural-history benchmark; any statement that single-arm response rates cannot establish superiority.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Identify short/absent durability follow-up as missing information precluding any cure claim.
candidate_requirements.rationale: The task requires distinguishing pathological response from durable cure; follow-up duration is the decisive missing datum.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Noting unknown recurrence-free or long-term survival outcomes; requesting median follow-up time.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Note that toxicity assessment is limited by small sample size and absence of a comparator, so the safety profile cannot be considered established.
candidate_requirements.rationale: Supports the required safety conclusion without inventing unreported toxicity data.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Stating that 'no grade ≥3 toxicity observed in 15 patients' is a weak safety signal.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Note that baseline staging details and standard-of-care comparison outcomes are not reported, limiting downstaging interpretation.
candidate_requirements.rationale: Downstaging percentages depend on baseline stage distribution, which is not supplied.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Requesting baseline TNM distribution or historical downstaging rates with standard care.
